title: fix(release): re-derive release-verify-npm read-back budget from the 18.0.0 reading (35 min, flat)
body:
Fixes #24888
Clause-②: no

`scripts/release-verify-npm.mjs` waited 15 minutes for npm's read path to settle. On 18.0.0 the last package became readable 16m22s after the first read, so a release that was complete read red. This PR re-derives the budget from the 18.0.0 reading and sets it to **35 minutes, one flat number for the group**. It still fails closed. The self-test now replays the 18.0.0 window on npm's own clock and pins `main()`'s exit code.

## The measurements, re-read

| Reading | Source | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Publish job | Actions API, job 118624531794 (run 39421537775, head `3fbef41b4a`) | 12:24:14Z to 12:57:40Z, failure |
| Step 21, "Publish to npm + push version tags" | same | 12:36:08Z to 12:57:38Z, failure; steps 22 and 23 skipped |
| The verdict | check-run annotations of job 118624531794 | `publish ran but 1 of 73 package(s) are still not readable on npm after 19 round(s) over 900s: @objectstack/console@18.0.0` |
| `console` readable | `npm view @objectstack/console time --json` | `"18.0.0": "2026-10-20T12:57:59.327Z"` |
| Verification start | the card's reading of the job log | 12:41:37Z |

**The start time is not re-read here.** The job-log download redirects to a blob host that this container's egress proxy refuses (403, a policy denial, not retried). The readings above corroborate it:
- 900 s of waits that end at 12:57:38Z put the start at or before 12:42:38Z.
- Replaying the 19 rounds against npm's `time` for all 73 packages gives 408 probes. The card's start implies 61 s of probing, about 150 ms per probe.

**Spread: 12:41:37Z to 12:57:59.327Z = 982.3 s (16m22s).**

**Sizes** come from npm's `dist` fields and the tarball bytes, downloaded:

| Package | Packed | Unpacked | Files | Readable at |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `@objectstack/console` | 9,399,458 B | 37,040,621 B | 2282 | +16m22s (last) |
| `@objectstack/spec` | 42,118,133 B | 197,756,260 B | 2100 | +10m04s |

The card's "42424 KB" for `console` lives in the job log, so it could not be re-read. It is not `console`'s tarball, which is 9.4 MB. The release's largest tarball is `spec`'s.

## Shape: flat, 35 minutes. The deciding axis: actual business need (实际业务需求)

**Derivation.** 17.3.0's margin was 900 s / 427 s = 2.11x. The same margin over the new spread is 982.3 s x 2.11 = 2070 s (34m30s). Rounded up, that is 35 minutes (2100 s, 2.14x the 18.0.0 spread). The header records this next to the 17.3.0 derivation.

| Axis | Flat budget | Size-scaled allowance per package |
|---|---|---|
| **Actual business need (实际业务需求), measured: decides** | Covers the group's spread, which is what the 18.0.0 red was. | Its premise is that the slow package was slow because it is large. The measurement says otherwise: `spec` (42.1 MB packed, the largest) was readable six minutes **before** `console` (9.4 MB). On 17.5.0 the order was reversed (`console` 08:05:24Z, `spec` last at 08:09:33Z), and on 17.3.0 the last package was `runtime`. Any monotonic size scale gives the slowest 18.0.0 package a smaller allowance than one that settled six minutes earlier. |
| Long-term soundness (项目长远合理性) | One constant, re-derived from readings recorded in the header. | Adds a second model (size to latency) that has no reading behind it and would need its own re-derivation. |
| Guarding against AI mistakes (防 AI 写代码犯错) | One number that a reader can check against the header. | Needs the size of a package the registry cannot serve yet, so the size has to come from a new local input. Each missing or wrong size becomes a per-package fallback, which is the lenient direction. |
| No scope spread at startup stage (创业阶段不扩散需求) | Changes one constant. | Adds a new mechanism and a new input. |

**The budget is a ceiling, not a wait.** The loop returns on the first round that finds the last target, so a good publish pays only its own settle time. Replayed on this schedule, 18.0.0 goes green at +17m15s (battery 14 pins that figure). Only a publish that is really broken spends all 35 minutes.

## Fit against the caller

`release.yml` was read, not edited. Neither the `publish` job (`:1565` to `:2132`) nor its step "Publish to npm + push version tags" declares `timeout-minutes`. The only `timeout-minutes` in the file is `full-battery`'s 10, at `:1536`. GitHub's default therefore bounds both: 360 minutes per job. The `release-integrity` audit calls the script with `--probe` (`:1251`). That path passes a budget of 0 and is unchanged; battery 10 pins its single round.

Measured on 18.0.0:

| Segment | Time |
|---|---|
| Before step 21 (build 4m44s, vendored Console SPA 5m44s) | 11m54s |
| Step 21 before verification (`pnpm run release`: publish plus tag push) | 5m29s |
| Verification at the old budget | 16m01s (900 s of waits plus about 61 s of probing) |
| Steps 22 and 23 on a green run | 1m55s: 1m48s plus 7s, measured on the same two scripts in the backfill, run 39426677839, job 118640898073 |

Worst case under the new budget, using budget plus poll interval plus the rest of the step:

| Term | Value |
|---|---|
| Waits | exactly 2100 s (38 waits, 39 rounds); battery 1 pins that the schedule sums to the budget |
| Poll interval | 60 s, the cap |
| Probing when **nothing** reached npm | 39 rounds x 73 probes x 150 ms = 427 s (7m07s) |
| Rest of the step | 5m29s |
| **Step** | 5m29s + 35m00s + 1m00s + 7m07s = **48m36s** |
| **Job** | 11m54s + 48m36s + 1m55s = **62m25s, against 360 minutes: 297 minutes of margin (5.8x)** |

The same terms at the old budget gave 38m46s.

One case lies outside that formula and existed before this change: a registry where every request hangs to the 15 s per-request ceiling. Each round then costs 73 x 15 s = 18m15s. That totals 347 minutes of probing at the old 19 rounds and 712 minutes at the new 39. In both cases GitHub's 360-minute default cancels the job. The job is red, so the run still fails closed, but the cancellation does not name a package. The outcome is the same before and after this change.

## Self-test and ablation

The self-test goes from 115 cases across 13 batteries to **131 cases across 14 batteries**, with every battery floored.

**Battery 1** gains two cases: the budget outlasts the 18.0.0 spread, and it keeps the 2.11x margin over it.

**Battery 14** ("The 18.0.0 publish window: console readable at +16m22s, past the old 900 s") has 14 cases. It replays npm's own `time` for `sdui-parser`, `cli`, `spec` and `console` on a clock that the stub `sleep` drives. Probing is taken as instant, so a green in the replay is one the real step would also have seen. No case sleeps.
- The old budget (900 s, passed as a parameter) reds and names only `console`, after 19 rounds over 900 s, which matches the run's annotation. Its last read of `console` came before `console` landed.
- The production budget is never passed in, so it is the default. It goes green on the first round after `console` landed, at +17m15s, past the round where 900 s ran out.
- **A package readable after 900 s and before the new budget passes:** `main()` over a fixture workspace exits 0 and prints the `::notice::` line.
- **An absent package exits non-zero and is named:** with `console` never landing, `main()` exits 1. Its `::error::` line names `@objectstack/console@18.0.0` and "1 of 4", and names none of the three packages that landed. It concludes only after the waits sum to exactly `RETRY_BUDGET_MS`.

This needed one seam change. `main()` now accepts the verifier's own `probe` and `sleep` seams; the defaults are the production ones. Its exit code and naming can therefore be pinned without the network or a real wait.

The case of a large and a small package, each held to its own allowance, does not apply, because there is no per-package allowance.

**Ablation.** I committed the fix first (`a9e61579a3`). I then ran `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode, replacing `export const RETRY_BUDGET_MS = 35 * 60 * 1000;` with `15 * 60 * 1000;`.
- Proof that the mutation landed: anchor count went from 1 to 0, replacement count from 0 to 1, blob `7f259d67ff62` became `c36e8cf51a07`.
- `node scripts/release-verify-npm.mjs --self-test` then exited 1 with **8 of 131 cases failed**, exactly the cases that need more than 900 s (one JSON detail is shortened):

```text
  x the budget outlasts the 16m22s spread measured on the 18.0.0 burst -- 900000 > 982327
  x and keeps the 17.3.0 margin (2.11x) over it -- 900000 >= 2070478 (0.92x)
  x THIS BUDGET sits through the 16m22s spread and goes GREEN -- {"ok":false,"missing":[{"name":"@objectstack/console",...}],"rounds":19,"waitedMs":900000,"checked":4}
  x ...on a round the old budget never reached -- waited=900000
  x ...the FIRST round after console landed, not by spending the budget -- 2026-10-20T12:55:52.000Z .. 2026-10-20T12:56:37.000Z
  x ...at +17m15s, the figure the header quotes -- waited=900000
  x main() exits 0 on the 18.0.0 replay, under the production budget -- code=1 ::error::publish ran but 1 of 4 package(s) are still not readable on npm after 19 round(s) over 900s: @objectstack/console@18.0.0
  x ...and its notice says the whole group settled --   1 of 4 package(s) not readable yet after round 18; waiting 45s (900s of 900s budget spent).
x release-verify-npm self-test: 8 of 131 case(s) failed.
```

The red went in the expected direction. The old-budget repro and the absent-package cases stayed green, as they should.

The restore was proven on disk: the blob after the restore equals the HEAD blob (`7f259d67ff62`), `git diff HEAD` was empty and `git status --porcelain` printed nothing.

## Changeset: `skip-changeset`, measured

`scripts/release-verify-npm.mjs` belongs to the root package `@objectstack/spec-monorepo`, which is `private: true` and has no `files`. No non-private workspace package lists a `files[]` entry under `scripts` or with `..`. No tracked symlink points into the root `scripts/`.

`git grep -l RETRY_BUDGET_MS` over `packages/**`, `apps/**` and `skills/**` returns 0 hits (exit 1). The positive control over `scripts/**` returns `scripts/release-verify-npm.mjs` (exit 0).

## Gates (local, at `a9e61579a3`)

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 33 commands for this one-file diff. All 33 ran and each exited 0, `check:pm-dispatch-gates` included (fast tier, 1913 cases).
- `--ran` reconciliation: `33 derived, 33 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`.
- `npx eslint --no-inline-config scripts/release-verify-npm.mjs` exited 0.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` at `origin/main` `78ab6474ca` exited 0. The commits since the base touch none of this script, `release-github-releases.mjs`, `workspace-enumerator.mjs` or `release.yml`.

CI owns the rest of the farm. `lint.yml`'s "Post-publish npm verification self-test" step runs this self-test.

## Acceptance notes

- **Stale comments in a governed file, not edited here.** Two comments in `.github/workflows/release.yml` still describe the old budget:
  - `:2077` to `:2080` says the verifier "retries with bounded backoff for 15 minutes, derived from ... 7m07s";
  - `:1236` says "instead of waited on for 15 minutes".

  Both now read stale. `.github/workflows/**` is governed, so this needs a separate comment-only edit if wanted. Carrier: none.
- **Pre-existing.** The hung-registry worst case above exceeds GitHub's 360-minute default at either budget, and is cancelled red without naming a package. This is an inference from the constants, not a reproduction. Carrier: none.
